gallery.filename: Plan of city during Battle of Seattle, 1856 (MOHAI 1791).jpg
gallery.title: File:Plan of city during Battle of Seattle, 1856 (MOHAI 1791).jpg
gallery.description:
During the early 1850s, hostility grew between the native peoples and the new settlers in the Puget Sound region. The "Decatur" and several other government ships were moved to the area to protect the settlers. On January 26, 1856, following word of a planned attack on Seattle, troops on the "Decatur" fired howitzers into the forest beyond Third Avenue where a group of angry Native Americans had gathered. The Indians retreated, burning buildings as they went.
This image shows a plan of Seattle at the time of this conflict. The U.S.S. Decatur is drawn off the coast.
Handwritten on mount: Plan of Seattle at time of Indian war Jan 1856.

Caption by MOHAI staff.

gallery.filename: Battle of Seattle map, January 1, 1856 - DPLA - ff9b8afdece6380426ca0e3d238eb7d0.jpg
gallery.title: File:Battle of Seattle map, January 1, 1856 - DPLA - ff9b8afdece6380426ca0e3d238eb7d0.jpg
gallery.description: Transcribed from photograph: "Battle of Seattle. Jan. 26, 1856. Plan of Seattle, 1855-6. Showing the position occupied by the Decatur's crew, Jan'y 26, together with the line of barricades erected and roads constructed. Drawn by Commodore T.S. Phelps. Redrawn by Mrs. Carl F. Gould. 1931." According to HistoryLink's article "Thomas Phelps's 1856 map of Seattle is published in the Town Crier on December 15, 1917": "Phelps's map depicts what has become known as the Battle of Seattle, when Native Americans battled settlers and the Decatur's crew on January 26, 1856. The death toll for the skirmish, which ended at 10 p.m., was two settlers and an unknown number of Indians. The map provides what appears to be an accurate depiction of the city on that day, although there is one notable mistake. The settlement's northern blockhouse, or fort, is in the wrong location; it should be two blocks south, at what is now Cherry Street. (Phelps also shows a southern blockhouse, which was not built until two weeks or so after the battle.) The only other map to depict Seattle around the time of the battle is a U.S. Coast Survey map of "Duwamish Bay, W.T." Published in 1854, it shows a roughly similar landscape and distribution of buildings."

gallery.description: Annual Christmas Number. Page 17 features advertisement for Carolina Court Apartments on Eastlake Ave. Page 23 article "The New Chief" discusses new Seattle Chief of Police, Joel Warren. Page 26 article "Seattle's First Taste of Warfare" discusses the Battle of Seattle in 1856. Page 27 article "Work in Hand to Be Done" discusses Seattle War Efforts. Page 32 includes photographs of Horace C. Henry's private art gallery. Page 33 article ""Some Seattle Artists and Their Work"" features artwork by local artists such as Edward Forkner, F.J. Crooks, Herbert Webb, Roy Partridge, Spiro Orfans, E. Frere Champney, Sara Visonhaler, F. Tadama, Imogen Cunningham Partridge, Irene Ewing, Gertrude Little, Kathleen Houlahan, Clare Shepard, Hamilton Wolf and Yasushi Tanaka. Page 79 features photograph of soldiers marching on 2nd Ave.
